titulo: The imperative: Recipes, warnings and requests

aula.objetivo: Give instructions, ask for things, and invite people with the affirmative imperative of «tú», «usted», «vosotros», and «ustedes», learn the eight irregular «tú» forms (ven, di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten), form the negative imperative with «no» + subjunctive, and place pronouns correctly.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: step-by-step instructions (recipes, manuals) use the «tú» or «usted» imperative, in short sentences: «Corta las patatas», «Fríe el huevo». STEP 2: asking for something: the imperative with «por favor» is correct, but a question is often preferred to sound friendlier: «¿Puedes cerrar la puerta?» instead of «Cierra la puerta». STEP 3: inviting: the imperative is warm here, not a command: «Pasa», «Siéntate», «Come un poco más». STEP 4: words to get someone's attention in formal settings: «oiga» (excuse me, with «usted»), «perdone» or «disculpe» (sorry/excuse me), and «mire» (look). STEP 5: on signs and notices, the infinitive is used instead of the imperative: «Empujar», «Tirar», «No fumar», «Cerrar la puerta» — a genuinely different habit from English, which puts signs in the imperative too ("Push," "Pull," "No smoking") but Spanish prefers the plain infinitive form. STEP 6: watch two confusing look-alikes: «ve» is the imperative of «ir» («Ve a casa») and also of «ver» («Ve esta película»); context sorts it out. And «sal» is the imperative of «salir» («Sal ahora») and also means table salt. STEP 7: in Spain, «coge» (from coger) means "grab/catch," but in parts of Latin America the verb has a vulgar sense; to be safe everywhere, use «toma» or «agarra» instead. And remember that «pegar» in Spanish means to hit or to glue — never "to grab" or "to catch," even though it might look like it should. STEP 8: with «ustedes», the imperative works for any group: «Pasen, por favor.» In Spain, among friends, it's «Pasad».
blocos.comparacao: English also uses the imperative on signs ("Push," "No smoking"), so that habit transfers fine — Spanish's preference for the bare infinitive instead («Empujar», «No fumar») is the one adjustment to make. The real trap is «pegar», which looks close enough to "peg" or could be mistaken for "to grab" — it actually means to hit or to glue. To say "grab it," reach for «toma» or «agarra» instead.

tabela.exemplo: [misto] Corta las patatas en trozos pequeños.
tabela.traducao: [misto] Cut the potatoes into small pieces.

erros.motivo: «Pegar» means to hit or to glue; for "grab," use «tomar».
Signs and notices usually use the infinitive.
The imperative «ve» carries no accent (but «sé», from «ser», does).

blocos.ru: Para hacer una tortilla de patatas para cuatro personas necesitas patatas, huevos, aceite y sal. Primero pela las patatas y córtalas en trozos pequeños. Pon aceite en una sartén y fríe las patatas a fuego suave. Mientras tanto, bate seis huevos en un plato grande con un poco de sal. Cuando las patatas estén blandas, sácalas del aceite y mézclalas con los huevos. Espera cinco minutos. Después pon la mezcla otra vez en la sartén y espera un poco. Cuando esté dorada por un lado, dale la vuelta con un plato. No tengas miedo: con práctica, saldrá bien. Cuando esté lista, sírvela caliente o fría.
blocos.pt: To make a potato tortilla for four people, you need potatoes, eggs, oil, and salt. First peel the potatoes and cut them into small pieces. Put oil in a pan and fry the potatoes on low heat. Meanwhile, beat six eggs in a large bowl with a little salt. When the potatoes are soft, take them out of the oil and mix them with the eggs. Wait five minutes. Then put the mixture back in the pan and wait a bit. When it's golden on one side, flip it using a plate. Don't be afraid: with practice, it'll turn out well. When it's ready, serve it hot or cold.

perguntas.pergunta: [misto] ¿Qué haces cuando está dorada por un lado?
perguntas.resposta: [misto] Le das la vuelta con un plato.

blocos.enunciado: Explain to a friend, using «tú» imperatives, how to make a simple dish you know. Give at least six steps.
Say the «tú» negative imperative of «hacer», «decir», «ir», and «ser». Then say four sentences with it.
